transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Spectra Head of ML), Jason Cole (Spectra Infra Eng), Marta Ruiz (Spectra CTO)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to understand Spectra's latency and throughput SLOs for realtime fraud-detection models. Discussed p95 goals, concurrency, streaming, token/sec benchmarks, and security constraints (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Agreed to run a short benchmark with Spectra's tokenized prompts and share pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Topics: p95 targets, concurrency (req/s & tokens/sec), streaming vs non-streaming, prefix/KV cache, batching, quantization, private VPC deployment, SOC2/KMS

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm ava from Redwood, i'll kick us off, we got liam from se here too, hi liam
[00:07] Liam Chen: hey all, hi priya, jason, marta, excited to dig in
[00:12] Priya Nair: thanks ava, quick context, we're building a realtime fraud scoring service. p95 latency needs to be ~120 ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), and ~300 ms for longer, with bursts up to 600 concurrent requests. that's sort of our target but we're flexible
[00:30] Marta Ruiz: and security is huge, we need VPC/private option, KMS for key management, SOC 2 compliance, and audit logs for every inference
[00:45] Jason Cole: also want to understand dedicated capacity vs hosted — we prefer predictable latency, so reserved GPUs sounds attractive, but cost is a concern
[00:58] Liam Chen: got it. so p95 120 ms short prompt, 300 ms longer, 600 concurrency bursts. that maps well to what we see with low-latency models. couple quick clarifying q's — what model families are you planning to use? custom fine-tuned Llama variants or closed models?
[01:15] Priya Nair: mostly an open LLM baseline we've finetuned, 13b-ish, some 70b experiments later, but we want to keep costs low. We also stream partial responses for scoring to get early signals
[01:28] Ava Martinez: streaming changes things — it reduces time to first token but can affect throughput. we do continuous batching and prefix/KV cache to help with repeated prefixes — will that help your usecase?
[01:43] Priya Nair: yes we have predictable prefixes for certain flows, so caching could cut repeated token work substantially
[01:50] Liam Chen: for dedicated vs hosted: dedicated gives you pinned GPU pools, predictable latency, and isolation — good for 600 concurrent p95 SLO. hosted can do burst capacity but is multi-tenant and has different tail behavior. we can quantify with a tokens/sec benchmark we run on your sample payloads
[02:12] Jason Cole: how should we think about token/sec? like do we measure it per GPU, per model? our infra team wants a clear tokens/sec per GPU number for capacity planning
[02:20] Liam Chen: recommend measuring tokens/sec at your typical prompt lengths and batching settings. we report both tokens/sec and effective request/sec at target p95. e.g. for 13b on A100-ish hardware with quantization we see ~X tokens/sec per GPU in our internal benchmarks (note: placeholder figure discussed) — we can run the exact numbers on your payload
[02:44] Priya Nair: what's the impact of quantization on score quality? we can't degrade precision too much for fraud false positives
[02:52] Ava Martinez: yep that's a common tradeoff; our Optimize tooling recommends quantization profiles per workload — we can run evals on your prompts to show quality delta vs latency/cost
[03:06] Marta Ruiz: and for private deployment, what's the control plane visibility? we need audit logs and console access, but network has to be customer-managed
[03:16] Liam Chen: Private option has a customer-managed network (VPC), we integrate with KMS/HSM for key management, and we expose audit logs and telemetry. the same runtime and APIs apply so migration is straightforward
[03:27] Jason Cole: on encryption at rest/in flight — do you have details for our security team? SAML SSO and RBAC as well
[03:33] Ava Martinez: yes SOC 2 + SSO/SAML + RBAC, we'll share the security pack. also detailed network diagrams for private
[03:39] Priya Nair: okay practical: can we do a short benchmark? we want p95 numbers and tokens/sec across 1, 50, 200, 600 concurrent clients, short vs long prompts, streaming vs non-streaming
[03:52] Liam Chen: absolutely — propose we run a 1-2 hour benchmark: we'll provision dedicated nodes (or hosted snapshot) to mirror your config, run your payloads, collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and breakdowns per token types. we'll share a spreadsheet with results
[04:10] Jason Cole: do you support client-side load generation scripts? we'd prefer to run the test from our infra so it's realistic
[04:16] Liam Chen: yes we can share pip package + k6 scripts, and also run the server-side if you want. we'll coordinate network egress rules
[04:25] Ava Martinez: for pricing, we'll send both hosted per-token and dedicated reserved capacity estimates, including burst pricing and a sample cost-per-1M tokens at your expected mixing of short/long prompts
[04:36] Marta Ruiz: timeline wise — we'd like benchmarks this month, decision in next 3–4 weeks. can you make that schedule?
[04:44] Ava Martinez: yes. we'll aim to get a benchmark run scheduled within 7 business days
[04:48] Priya Nair: great. quick nit: does your runtime support KV cache invalidation? we have dynamic keys
[04:55] Liam Chen: yes cache invalidation hooks exist, and we can expose a TTL + manual invalidation API. small caveat: invalidations can increase tail latency briefly
[05:07] Priya Nair: noted. also do you provide model rollouts/canarying? we need gradual rollouts when switching quantization profiles
[05:14] Ava Martinez: yes rollouts and A/B traffic split, automatic fallback policies if a variant crosses error or latency thresholds
[05:23] Jason Cole: any competitors or gotchas we should be aware of? we've looked at Anthropic and OpenAI managed endpoints and self-hosting on-prem
[05:31] Liam Chen: common tradeoffs: Anthropic/OpenAI give easy managed access but cost and limited private options; self-hosting gives control but ops burden. Redwood tries to hit middle ground: runtime + ops to reduce your bur-en
[05:46] Marta Ruiz: on SLA — what p95 guarantees do you provide for Dedicated? and what about multi-region fallbacks?
[05:53] Liam Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets we can include in the contract, and smart routing can fallback to another region or a compatible variant if capacity is constrained. we'll surface the specific p95 targets per contract
[06:06] Priya Nair: excellent. For the benchmark payload — we'll share sample logs and a set of 5000 prompts, with labels and expected scoring latency thresholds
[06:17] Ava Martinez: perfect. recap: we'll email pricing and security docs, liam will prepare benchmark plan and scripts, priya will share payloads and targets, schedule benchmark next week. anything else?
[06:30] Marta Ruiz: nothing from me — thanks all
[06:33] Jason Cole: thanks
[06:35] Ava Martinez: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with action items, talk soon

Recap & Next Steps (auto): Send pricing + security docs; schedule benchmark; Spectra to share prompts and p95 targets; Redwood to prepare scripts and run 1-2 hour tokens/sec benchmark. Action items captured above.

Notes: transcription contains minor errors and speaker overlaps; some technical terms transcribed approximately (KV cache, KMS, quantization). Links referenced: security pack (link sent via email), benchmark spreadsheet (link to be shared).
